description: AI/ML engine: packaging knowledge base, rule-based scoring engine, explainability module, ML training pipeline, and the unified recommendation engine. Depends on FEAT-001 (needs models/schemas). Independent of FEAT-003 (routes).
steps: Create backend/app/ai/knowledge_base.py: A Python dict/dataclass structure defining 20+ packaging materials with their barrier scores, cost index, sustainability attributes, food compatibility rules, and typical use cases. Materials to include: LDPE, HDPE, PP, BOPP, PET, Metallized PET, Aluminium Foil, Paperboard, Kraft Paper, Glass, PET Bottle, HDPE Bottle, PLA, Biodegradable Film, Multilayer PE/PA, EVOH Multilayer, Nylon (PA), PVC (restricted), Vacuum Pouches (PA/PE), MAP Film. Each entry includes: material_code, moisture_barrier (0-1), oxygen_barrier (0-1), light_barrier (0-1), thermal_resistance (0-1), mechanical_strength (0-1), cost_index (0-1 where 1=most expensive), recyclable (bool), biodegradable (bool), food_contact_safe (bool), suitable_categories (list of FoodCategory values), unsuitable_for (list of restrictions e.g. 'high_fat'), description, typical_thickness_range (tuple of um values).

Create backend/app/ai/rule_engine.py: RuleEngine class with method filter_candidates(food_profile, storage_conditions, packaging_requirements) -> list[str] (material_codes). Rules: (1) eliminate any material with food_contact_safe=False; (2) if food has high moisture sensitivity, require moisture_barrier >= 0.6; (3) if food has high oxygen sensitivity, require oxygen_barrier >= 0.7; (4) if food has high light sensitivity, require light_barrier >= 0.5; (5) if cold_chain NOT required and storage_temp > 30, require thermal_resistance >= 0.5; (6) if eco_preference is 'biodegradable', prefer bio/PLA materials but do not eliminate all others; (7) category-specific rules (e.g., beverages require bottle/PET types). Returns at least 3 candidates always by relaxing constraints if too few pass.

Create backend/app/ai/scoring_engine.py: ScoringEngine class with method score_material(material_code, food_profile, storage_conditions, packaging_requirements) -> dict with keys: moisture_score, oxygen_score, light_score, thermal_score, mechanical_score, food_safety_score, shelf_life_score, cost_score, sustainability_score, overall_score (all 0-100). Scoring is deterministic: each dimension computed from the material's barrier property vs the food's sensitivity level (low=0.3, medium=0.6, high=0.9) multiplied by 100. overall_score = weighted average using priority weights: balanced (equal), low_cost (cost_score 40%), max_shelf_life (shelf_life_score 35%), food_safety (food_safety_score 35%), sustainability (sustainability_score 35%).

Create backend/app/ai/explainer.py: Explainer class with method generate_explanation(primary_material, scores, food_profile, storage_conditions, packaging_requirements) -> str. Produces a 3-5 sentence human-readable explanation of WHY this material was chosen. Must reference: the top 2 scoring dimensions, the food's key sensitivities, shelf-life suitability, and sustainability note. Also generate_risk_factors(material, food_profile) -> list[str] returning 2-4 concrete risk statements.

Create backend/app/ai/recommendation_engine.py: RecommendationEngine class combining RuleEngine, ScoringEngine, Explainer. Method recommend(food_profile, storage_conditions, packaging_requirements) -> RecommendationResult dataclass. Steps: (1) filter candidates via rule_engine; (2) score each candidate; (3) sort by overall_score desc; (4) primary = top candidate, alternatives = next 2-3; (5) compute packaging_structure string (e.g. 'Single-layer BOPP 25µm' or 'Multilayer PET/PE 80µm'); (6) generate barrier_properties dict; (7) compute shelf_life_min/max from material properties and food perishability; (8) call explainer for explanation and risk_factors. RecommendationResult has all fields matching Recommendation ORM model. This is the single entry point called by recommendation_service.py.

Create ml/dataset/synthetic_data.py: Generates 500 synthetic training records covering all food categories and material combinations. Each record has: food_category (encoded int), moisture_content, ph, fat_content, water_activity, respiration_rate, oxygen_sensitivity (0/1/2), moisture_sensitivity (0/1/2), light_sensitivity (0/1/2), storage_temp, storage_duration_days, required_shelf_life_days, budget_index, priority_encoded — and target label: best_material_code (str) and overall_score (float). Saves to ml/dataset/training_data.csv. Uses numpy random seed 42 for reproducibility.

Create ml/preprocessing/preprocessor.py: PackagingPreprocessor class using sklearn Pipeline. Numerical features: StandardScaler. Categorical features: OneHotEncoder (handle_unknown='ignore'). Feature list matches synthetic_data.py columns. fit_transform(X) and transform(X) methods. Saves fitted preprocessor to ml/models/preprocessor.pkl using joblib.

Create ml/training/train_model.py: Loads ml/dataset/training_data.csv (runs synthetic_data.py if not present), fits preprocessor, trains RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42) to predict overall_score, trains a separate RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42) to predict best_material_code. Evaluates on 20% hold-out set (prints MAE and accuracy). Saves both models and preprocessor to ml/models/ using joblib. Prints 'Training complete. Models saved.'

Create ml/prediction/predictor.py: PackagingPredictor class. __init__ loads ml/models/packaging_model.pkl and ml/models/preprocessor.pkl (gracefully falls back if not found — logs warning). predict(features_dict) -> dict with predicted_material_code and confidence_score. Used by recommendation_engine.py as an optional ML override — if the ML confidence > 0.8 it can influence the top recommendation, otherwise rule+scoring engine takes precedence.

findings: FEAT-003 notes: (1) RecommendationEngine.recommend() accepts plain dicts matching FoodProfileCreate, StorageConditionsInput, PackagingRequirementsInput schema fields — call .model_dump() on Pydantic objects before passing. (2) RecommendationResult.to_dict() returns all fields needed to populate the Recommendation ORM row; primary_material_id must be resolved from primary_material_code by DB lookup in the service. (3) alternative_material_codes is a list[str] of material_codes (not IDs) — service must look up IDs. (4) barrier_properties and risk_factors are plain Python dicts/lists — serialize with json.dumps() before writing to Text columns. (5) all_scores in RecommendationResult is extra frontend data; store as JSON in barrier_properties or ignore when writing ORM row. (6) ml/models/ directory contains packaging_model.pkl, score_model.pkl, preprocessor.pkl — generated at startup or via train_model.py; ML override is optional and gracefully disabled when files absent. (7) Python 3.14 environment — all imports verified working. (8) ScoringEngine and RuleEngine are stateless; safe to instantiate once at app startup and reuse.
